brief: A private physiotherapy practice in Leeds with four practitioners, treating people with long-running back and knee pain after referral or self-referral.

sources.note: I have had back pain for months and I do not know whether physiotherapy will help. I want to check the physiotherapist is properly registered before I give my details. I would rather write than phone because I am at work. I need to know what the first appointment involves and what it costs before I commit.
The practice window carries slate blue lettering on pale grey glass, with rounded corners on the door plate and a plain humanist typeface.
sources.lettering: Plain humanist lettering with rounded corners on the door plate.

sources.note: All four practitioners appear on the Health and Care Professions Council register under their own names, and the practice is registered with the major insurers.

statement.object: whether a private physiotherapy practice can help long-running back pain
statement.context: before giving their details and paying for a first appointment

functional.value: They have had back pain for months and need to know whether physiotherapy will help and what the first appointment involves.

emotional.value: They worry about giving their details to a practice that may not be properly registered.

social.value: They are at work and cannot phone, so they need a way to ask in writing.

consideration.because: The pain has lasted months and they want to check registration, the first appointment and the cost before they commit.

objections: not knowing whether physiotherapy will help
whether the physiotherapist is properly registered
language: I want to check the physiotherapist is properly registered
I would rather write than phone because I am at work

primaryAction.because: The considered job is a patient at work who would rather write than phone, so an enquiry is offered in the header and again once they have checked whether the physiotherapist is properly registered.

order.because: A patient with months of back pain first needs to see that the practice treats back pain and what the first appointment involves.
They do not know whether physiotherapy will help, so the conditions treated come before who treats them.
They want to check the physiotherapist is properly registered, so the practitioners come with their register details.
They need to know what the first appointment costs before they commit, so the fee sits before the ask.
Once registration and cost are clear, a patient at work can write to the practice.

lead.value: Help with long-running back and knee pain
lead.because: Months of back pain is the reason a visitor is here, so it leads ahead of the other conditions the practice treats.

journey.because: A visitor with months of back pain first needs to see the practice treats it.
Before giving their details, they want to check the physiotherapist is properly registered.
Once registration and the first appointment cost are clear, they can write because they cannot phone from work.

proof.what: each practitioner's name and Health and Care Professions Council register entry
proof.because: The visitor wants to check the physiotherapist is properly registered, so the register entry is shown as plain text with a link to the public register.

proof.what: a short line in the hero saying all practitioners are registered
proof.because: A visitor worried about registration meets the answer on the first screen and can read the detail in the team section.

proof.what: practitioner names, specialisms and years in practice, with no portraits
proof.because: A patient choosing who to see wants names and specialisms for their back pain, which a written profile gives without a portrait.

proof.what: a summary of patient-reported progress after treatment for back pain
proof.because: A visitor who does not know whether physiotherapy will help would be reassured by seeing how patients with back pain progressed, if the practice can show it.

accent.because: The practice window carries slate blue lettering, so the same slate blue colour marks the enquiry button.

ground.because: The practice window has pale grey glass behind its lettering, so the page ground follows that glass.

display.because: The plain humanist lettering on the practice window gives headlines the same open forms.

body.because: The plain humanist lettering on the practice window keeps supporting text open and easy to read.

shape.because: The door plate on the practice window has rounded corners, so the buttons keep them.
